precepts.text: I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels; the promised king comes out of David's bowels.
precepts.point: In Isaiah 7 Ahaz would not ask a sign, so the Lord gave one: a virgin shall conceive and bear a son named Immanuel, and before the child knew to refuse the evil the land of the two kings, Syria and Ephraim, would be forsaken; the sign was the child.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.why:
The Lord promised David a king out of his own body: “And when thy days be fulfilled, and thou shalt sleep with thy fathers, I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom.”

The seed that proceeds out of David's bowels is the promised king. So when the angel came to Joseph in the dream, he called him “Joseph, thou son of David”. The line is Joseph's, David's line.

The angel said, “fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost.” That which is conceived in her is of the prophecy of 2 Samuel: the seed promised to David, coming out of his bowels.

That is why the Nativity begins with the bloodline. The child Mary conceived is the fulfilling of the promise made to David, that God would set up his seed after him and establish his kingdom.

precepts.text: Rather being good, I came into a body undefiled: Solomon's body was defiled and Christ's was not, and Solomon knew who he was.
precepts.point: So the Lord is speaking of Christ here, and what is being revealed in the same breath is who Solomon was.

precepts.text: I took thee from the sheepcote, from following the sheep, to be ruler over my people, over Israel; from literal sheep to shepherd over the sheep of the house of Israel.
precepts.point: Taking a keeper of sheep and making him the shepherd of the nation is a pattern with the Most High; he took leaders and prophets from following literal flocks and set them to feed the flock of Israel.

note.label: 1 Samuel 16: The Lord Looketh on the Heart

precepts.why:
Jesse made seven of his sons pass before Samuel, the older, bigger, more developed ones, and Samuel said, “The Lord hath not chosen these.” There remained “yet the youngest, and, behold, he keepeth the sheep.” Samuel would not sit down until he was fetched, and the Most High said, “Arise, anoint him: for this is he.”

The Lord sent word to David himself: “Thus saith the Lord of hosts, I took thee from the sheepcote, from following the sheep, to be ruler over my people, over Israel”. From literal sheep to shepherd over the sheep of the house of Israel. Taking a keeper of sheep and making him the shepherd of the nation is a pattern with the Most High.

precepts.text: The angel told Mary she should bring forth a son and call his name Jesus.
precepts.point: The Lord promised that His mercy would not depart from him as it did from Saul, and that David's house, kingdom, and throne would be established for ever. The Lord did not make the Bible easy in every place, that He might see who would research and learn precept upon precept.

note.label: 2 Samuel 7: The Covenant With the House of David

precepts.why:
The Lord told David, “I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom.” The word reaches past Solomon. The angel told Mary, “thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son, and shalt call his name JESUS.”

Solomon built the house and sat on the throne, but his kingdom was not established for ever. His son Rehoboam would not hear counsel, and the kingdom split into two nations. The seed whose kingdom is established for ever is Jesus Christ the black Messiah, who came through David's lineage.

precepts.text: The Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David; Christ came through David's lineage.
precepts.point: The Lord promised that His mercy would not depart from him as it did from Saul, and that David's house, kingdom, and throne would be established for ever. The Lord did not make the Bible easy in every place, that He might see who would research and learn precept upon precept.

note.label: 2 Samuel 7: The Covenant With the House of David

precepts.why:
“He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David.”

That is the promise to David fulfilled: “I will be his father, and he shall be my son.” Christ is called the Son of the Highest, and the Lord God gives him the throne of his father David. Christ came through David's lineage, and he is the seed the Lord spoke of when he said, “I will stablish the throne of his kingdom for ever.”

note.label: 2 Samuel 7: The Covenant With the House of David

precepts.why:
“And he shall reign over the house of Jacob for ever; and of his kingdom there shall be no end.”

The Lord told David, “thine house and thy kingdom shall be established for ever before thee: thy throne shall be established for ever.” Solomon's kingdom did end; it split into two nations under Rehoboam. The phrase “for ever” points to Christ, whose kingdom has no end. He reigns over the house of Jacob for ever.

precepts.text: They shall smite the judge of Israel with a rod upon the cheek; this was fulfilled in Christ, not Solomon.
precepts.point: The Lord promised that His mercy would not depart from him as it did from Saul, and that David's house, kingdom, and throne would be established for ever. The Lord did not make the Bible easy in every place, that He might see who would research and learn precept upon precept.

note.label: 2 Samuel 7: The Covenant With the House of David

precepts.why:
The Lord said of David's seed, “If he commit iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men, and with the stripes of the children of men.” Solomon was not chastened with the rod of men in his lifetime.

Micah shows who was: “they shall smite the judge of Israel with a rod upon the cheek.” That was fulfilled in Christ, not Solomon. Jesus the Christ was smitten with the rod upon the cheek, and he did no sin, though it was Solomon who sinned.

The Lord did not make the Bible easy in every place, that he might see who would research and learn precept upon precept.

precepts.text: Out of Bethlehem shall come forth the ruler in Israel, whose goings forth have been from everlasting.

note.label: 2 Samuel 7: The Covenant With the House of David

precepts.why:
“But thou, Beth–lehem Ephratah, though thou be little among the thousands of Judah, yet out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel; whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting.”

Out of Bethlehem, the city of David, comes the ruler in Israel. His goings forth have been from everlasting, and that is the one whose throne the Lord said “shall be established for ever.” The same judge of Israel smitten with a rod upon the cheek is the ruler who came forth out of Bethlehem: Jesus Christ, of David's line.

precepts.text: He will make them one nation, and one king shall be king to them all; no more two nations.
precepts.point: The northern and southern kingdoms are to be made one nation again under one king and one shepherd. The one king is Jesus Christ, called the throne of David because David ruled over all twelve tribes; David will be present but is not the king. The chief shepherd, the great shepherd, the good shepherd who lays down his life is Christ, and he gathers the elect from the four winds and brings them up out of the land.

note.label: 2 Samuel 7: The Covenant With the House of David

precepts.why:
David asked, “what one nation in the earth is like thy people, even like Israel, whom God went to redeem for a people to himself”? The Most High did not redeem one man alone but a whole people, and he will bring them out again as a people.

Ezekiel shows how: “I will make them one nation in the land upon the mountains of Israel; and one king shall be king to them all: and they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all.” The northern and southern kingdoms are to be made one nation again under one king.

The teaching applies to us now. Though a brother or sister may have a difference, we must forgive one another and come back together, for the Most High chose us as one people. We lost our heritage in captivity, and coming back to it we must let go of grudges.

note.label: 2 Samuel 7: The Covenant With the House of David

precepts.why:
“And David my servant shall be king over them; and they all shall have one shepherd.” The one king is Jesus Christ. He is called David, and called the throne of David, because he comes of David's line and David ruled over all twelve tribes. David will be present, but he is not the king.

That is the house the Lord spoke of to David “for a great while to come”, and why David sat before the Lord and said, “Who am I, O Lord God? and what is my house, that thou hast brought me hitherto?” Under that one king and one shepherd, Israel “shall also walk in my judgments, and observe my statutes, and do them.”

The children of Judah, the southern kingdom, and the children of Israel, the northern kingdom, are gathered together under one head, and that head is Christ. David said, “thou hast confirmed to thyself thy people Israel to be a people unto thee for ever.” The same people he redeemed from Egypt he gathers again and brings up out of the land.

Christ is the one who brings Israel up. The Most High redeemed Israel from Egypt, “from the nations and their gods”, and he will do it again: the one king and one shepherd gathers the elect from the four winds and brings them up out of the land.

The God of peace brought him again from the dead, and he is the one shepherd over Israel, made one nation again. That is what the Lord meant when he told David he had spoken of his house “for a great while to come.”

precepts.text: I will set up thy seed and establish his kingdom; he shall build a house and his throne shall be established forever.
precepts.point: Solomon was set up after David and built the house, but the throne established forever refers to Christ. Solomon committed much iniquity and was not chastened with the rod of men; this points to something deeper in Christ.

note.label: Psalm 132: The Oath to David and the Throne Forever

precepts.why:
“The Lord hath sworn in truth unto David; he will not turn from it; Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne.” Here is the oath: “I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom. He shall build an house for my name, and I will stablish the throne of his kingdom for ever. I will be his father, and he shall be my son. If he commit iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men, and with the stripes of the children of men”.

Solomon was set up after David and built the house, but the throne established for ever refers to Christ. Solomon committed much iniquity and was not chastened with the rod of men, so this points to something deeper in Christ. David’s seed will sit on the throne for evermore, as it has been prophesied.

precepts.text: The Most High would set up David's seed that proceeds out of his bowels and establish the throne of his kingdom forever, which is Christ's everlasting kingdom.
precepts.point: "Like unto thee," like unto Moses, means the same similarities: Moses spoke to the Most High directly, mediated between the Most High and Israel, gave the laws, was hidden as a child when the young were sought to be killed, and led Israel toward the promised land.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:
The promise to David: “I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom. He shall build an house for my name, and I will stablish the throne of his kingdom for ever.”

The seed proceeds out of David's bowels, from the body of a man, and the throne of his kingdom is established for ever. That is Christ's everlasting kingdom, and it confirms that the prophet raised up from among the brethren came through the seed of man, David's seed.
